title: Inference on a Shared Causal Slope across Environments with Changing Non-Gaussian Sources
banked_reason: Delivered tier subfield below field floor; score ceiling 6.6 < 7.4; both panels pass and no bounded in-scope repair remains.
gap_reasons: The exact decision-error and false-retention constants in thm:binary-frontier are proved only for known Rademacher source laws and Gaussian noise.
A sharp unknown-source constant, a uniformly attaining feasible rule, and a lower bound matching the full-model confidence-set length remain open in oeq:unknown-source-efficiency.
The framing discloses those limits accurately, but their absence and the fixed-count quantitative stratum limit the projected leading-journal score.
proof_attempt_summary: The run proved the exact pooled fiber, honest short-component confidence sets on fixed quantitative strata, regular estimation after environmental label separation, and exact decision-error constants in a fully specified binary experiment. Two attempts at the unknown-source extension established only unprojected fixed-path LAN and likelihood-ratio results; they did not justify the nuisance-projected least-favorable distance or one uniformly attaining feasible rule. After removing a redundant non-Gaussianity assumption and revalidating every dependent proof, both panels passed, but the clean novelty review placed the package at subfield rather than the field floor.
tldr: Only the causal slope is shared across environments; source laws and confounding slopes may change. The established results recover the exact pooled causal-effect fiber, give honest sets with \(n^{-1/2}\) total length on each fixed quantitative stratum, yield regular estimation after environmental labels separate, and identify exact local decision-error constants in a fully specified binary experiment. The corresponding unknown-source efficiency constant and a single rule attaining it across smooth collision neighborhoods remain open.
gap: Known one-environment alias and cumulant results and structured environmental identification do not supply a uniform weak-label inference frontier under arbitrary simultaneous source-law and confounding-slope changes.
fill: Establish an observed-law fiber, an indexed short-component confidence procedure, a separated-label estimator, and a sharp specified-law binary benchmark.
